newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin stable in hospital, Kremlin says.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin stable in hospital, Kremlin says.

text.p: Boris Yeltsin's health "stabilised significantly" on Thursday, a Kremlin spokesman said, adding that the president, who is in hospital with pneumonia, had a normal temperature, blood pressure and other indicators.
"An X-ray has shown progress in curing the pneumonia," the spokesman told Reuters, reading from a prepared statement.
"The patient's condition has stabilised significantly. His temperature and blood pressure are normal," he said.
"Today the president worked on documents for two hours, paying special attention to preparing a state of the nation address to parliament."

The Kremlin statement added that Yeltsin's wife, Naina, who has also been ill, had been discharged from the Central Clinical Hospital. The president is expected to remain there for the rest of the week.

Yeltsin was taken into the elite clinic on January 8. Doctors say the pneumonia in both lungs has no direct link to the heart bypass operation he underwent last November. The chief Kremlin doctor warned on Wednesday that pneumonia was a serious condition which needed careful treatment.
